summary: Add provider-neutral tenant feature entitlements and atomic UTC-window quotas without hard-coded subscription-plan branches or a Cloud Billing runtime dependency.

impacts.evidence: Rules, quota policies, counters and usage are organization/workspace scoped with composite workspace foreign keys, transaction-local tenant settings and forced RLS.
Quota usage stores only metric, amount, correlation and policy identity; feature evaluation and API responses are no-store and contain no customer content or credentials.
An additive POST /entitlements/evaluate API and Draft 2020-12 schemas are added. Existing billing subscription contracts are unchanged.
Two additive governance.entitlement.* v1 events are emitted through the existing outbox; no published event is modified.
Connector SDK root interfaces and provider admission are unchanged. Future connectors may consume host entitlement guards without SDK plan branches.
Expand migration 000018 adds entitlement rules, quota policies, counters and append-only usage with no destructive rename/drop.
Feature and quota evaluation fail closed. Quota consumption serializes immutable usage IDs and locks counters; RLS prevents cross-tenant policy or usage access.
Task 028 does not replace Task 017 approvals; a caller may require both entitlement authorization and approval for sensitive operations.
Rule and quota-policy mutations atomically append Task-003 audit, Task-008 outbox and Task-030 lineage evidence with exact version identity.
Quota consumption requires immutable usage IDs; identical retries are idempotent and reuse with changed evidence fails closed. Counter mutation is transactional.
Task 028 adds no network path or webhook delivery behavior.
Evaluation returns stable reason codes and quota status exposes limit/used/remaining/window/policy version. SLO thresholds remain Task 066.
Migration is expand-only; binary rollback leaves policy and usage evidence intact. Deployment qualification must restore counters and usage consistently.
Tests cover deny-by-default, UTC window semantics, quota exceed behavior, no-consume-on-feature-deny, migration guardrails and a static no-plan-branch audit.
